transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What has brought you in to see me today?

Hi… thanks for seeing me. I guess the main thing is that I’m having trouble staying on track. It’s not like I’m trying to be careless or anything, but I’ll be working on something—like a dashboard I’m supposed to finish—and then one Slack ping, or even a song lyric or some random idea for another project, and I just lose the thread completely. It’s been happening enough that I thought I should probably talk to someone about it, if that makes sense.
When you think back over your life, have you had this kind of trouble staying focused and getting sidetracked since you were a kid, or is it more of a recent change for you?

I think it’s been around since I was little, yeah. I mean, I did okay in school, so I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but even in elementary school my teachers would write comments about me rushing through worksheets or missing parts of the directions.

And during group work I guess I would talk over people sometimes—not trying to be rude, just kind of jumping in. My parents also used to sit next to me when I did homework because otherwise I’d wander off or start doing something else before I finished. So… I don’t think it’s totally new. Does that answer what you mean?
Lately, do you find yourself feeling worried or tense much of the day, even about things that aren’t immediately going wrong?

Um… I don’t think so, not much of the day. I mean, I get stressed about normal stuff, like if I’m behind or I think I messed something up, but I wouldn’t say I’m just tense or worried all the time for no reason. At least, I haven’t really noticed that. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Outside of work, do these difficulties with staying focused or getting sidetracked also cause problems for you—for example in managing things like chores, errands, or personal projects?

Yeah… outside of work or school-type stuff, it does show up. I try not to make excuses for it, because I know everyone drops the ball sometimes, but for me it’s caused some real issues.

Like, I’ve had small freelance opportunities not really continue because I didn’t follow through cleanly enough, or I’d miss parts of what I was supposed to do. And there was a portfolio competition I wanted to enter, and I just… didn’t get it together in time. That one still bothers me.

I think people generally like my ideas, and my friends aren’t mean about it, but some of them are a little hesitant to collaborate with me now because they’re not sure I’ll be reliable. Which is embarrassing to say, but… yeah, it has affected things outside of just work.
Over the past few weeks, have you been feeling down or sad most days, even when nothing in particular has gone wrong?

I don’t think so… not most days. I mean, I have moments where I feel discouraged or kind of embarrassed about things, but I wouldn’t say I’m just sad for no reason or down all the time lately. At least not in a way that feels like the main issue, if that makes sense.
Right now in your current job, are these focus and follow‑through problems causing you clear trouble with your performance, like missed deadlines or feedback from your manager about reliability?

Well… I’m not actually in a current job right now, so I can’t really say it’s showing up with a manager or formal deadlines at the moment.

But in similar work-type things, like freelance or portfolio stuff, yeah, it has caused problems. I’ve lost a couple of small freelance opportunities because I didn’t follow through as cleanly as I should have, and I missed a portfolio competition I really wanted to enter because I just didn’t get everything together in time.

And… I think people do like my ideas, so I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but some friends or collaborators seem a little hesitant to work with me now because they’re not sure I’ll be reliable. Does that count as the kind of performance trouble you mean?

When you were a kid, did adults ever describe you as unusually restless or "hyper," like having trouble staying seated, always fidgeting, or seeming to be constantly on the go compared with other children?

Um… yeah, I think so. I don’t know if I was “hyper” in the really extreme way people picture, but even in elementary school my teachers would write comments about me rushing through worksheets or losing track of the directions.

I also talked over classmates during group work sometimes, which is… not great to admit. And my parents used to sit next to me while I did homework because if they didn’t, I’d wander off or start doing something else before I actually finished. Does that sound like the kind of thing you mean?

Thinking about your life right now, do you notice these same focus and follow‑through problems showing up in at least two different parts of your life, like for example both at home and in social or hobby situations?

Yeah… I think it does show up in more than one area, unfortunately. I don’t want to overstate it, because it’s not like everything is falling apart, but with my freelance or portfolio-type work I’ve lost a couple small opportunities because I didn’t follow through very smoothly. And I missed a portfolio competition I really wanted to enter because I just couldn’t get it all together in time.

Socially, or with friends I might collaborate with, I think it’s affected things too. People seem to like my ideas, which is nice, but I get the sense some of them are a little hesitant to count on me now. Like they’re not totally sure I’ll be reliable. Does that answer what you mean by different parts of life?

Right now, when you sit down to do something that requires sustained mental effort—like working on a project or filling out forms—do you often find yourself making careless mistakes or missing details even when you’re genuinely trying to do it carefully?

Yeah… I do, sometimes. I try to be careful, so it’s kind of embarrassing when it happens, but I’ll think something is basically polished—like a mockup or a data chart—and then later I’ll notice I mislabeled an axis or used the wrong color key.

Or I’ll realize I missed some tiny instruction in the brief that I thought I had read properly. It’s not like I’m not trying, which is the frustrating part. I usually feel like I am paying attention, and then some detail just slips through. Does that fit what you mean by careless mistakes?

Thinking back as clearly as you can, were these kinds of focus and follow‑through problems already noticeable in you before you turned 12 years old, rather than only starting later on in your teens or adulthood?

Yeah, I think they were there before 12. I mean, I don’t want to make it sound worse than it was, but in elementary school teachers did write comments about me rushing through worksheets or not keeping track of the directions.

And I remember during group work I’d sometimes talk over other kids, which I know isn’t great. At home, my parents would sit beside me while I did homework because otherwise I’d kind of drift off, wander away, or start something else before I actually finished. So… yes, I think it was noticeable then, not just something that started later.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports a longstanding pattern, beginning in childhood and clearly present before age 12, of inattention (careless mistakes, losing track of directions, difficulty sustaining focus, poor follow‑through) and some hyperactive/impulsive features (talking over others, needing close supervision to stay on task). These symptoms are currently present, cause clinically significant impairment (lost freelance work, missed competition, collaborators hesitant to rely on them), and occur across multiple domains (academic/freelance, home, social/collaborative settings). There is no evidence that anxiety, depression, or situational stress alone account for the symptoms. This supports a diagnosis of ADHD, predominantly inattentive type (F90.0). Z73.0 (burn‑out/state of vital exhaustion) was considered but is less likely given clear childhood onset and cross‑situational, trait‑like pattern rather than a recent, stress‑linked decline.
